s01_title: This is kay care sim. A simulated apartment where a home care robot runs its real software, and learns to open drawers with a vision language action model. In about five minutes, we go from a floor plan to the robot opening a drawer.
s02_problem: Testing on the real robot is slow. There is one robot, and every run needs a person next to it. A policy trained in the office opened only eight percent of the drawers in the house. Simulators look nothing like real cameras. And a simulator usually needs its own robot software. Kay care sim answers each of these.
s03_overview: There are three parts. Moo Joe Co simulates the apartment and the robot, behind the robot's own ROS two interfaces. The robot's kay care software connects to them unchanged, from the dashboard to the skills. And a trained policy runs on the GPU, served by v l a serve.
s04_house: Step one. The house. It follows the owner's floor plan, at two centimeters per unit, ten by eight meters. Furniture and textures come from photos of the real rooms. Where photos and the robot's own cameras disagree, the robot's cameras win.
s05_tour: Step two. The robot's software drives the simulated robot. Kay care sends the same navigation goals and arm commands it sends on the real robot. Here it visits the study, the kitchen and the bedroom, and finds an object at each place. Top left, the head camera. Top right, the wrist camera. Below, a follow camera and a fixed camera over the whole house. Playback is three times faster.
s06_cameras: Step three. Make the renders look like the cameras. Each image goes through lens distortion, auto exposure, white balance, saturation, noise and compression, plus motion blur. The parameters are fitted to the robot's own images. The first fit used one wood patch, and turned every white wall yellow. Fitting white balance on white and grey surfaces fixed it.
s07_depth: Depth is not perfect either. The wrist camera measures depth by stereo, so its noise grows with distance and it leaves holes on plain surfaces. The simulated sensor reproduces this, and matches the real noise up to about eighty centimeters.
s08_data: Step four. Training data. A scripted expert opens the top, middle or bottom drawer from the robot's real ready pose. Lighting, placement, camera settings and the cabinet's place in the house change every episode. Five hundred episodes take about two hours, with no failures.
s09_train: Step five. Train and evaluate. Small V L A is fine tuned from the office policy on office and house data, about one point four seconds per step. Every checkpoint is tested on the same fifty scenes. Before house training, the office policy opened four drawers out of fifty in the house.
s10_vla: Step six. The payoff. Kay care drives to the cabinet, then calls its open drawer skill. The skill sends a ROS action. The policy reads both cameras and the instruction, and returns fifty joint targets at a time, played at thirty hertz. The middle drawer opens by twenty eight point six centimeters, in eighteen point seven seconds.
s11_results: The results. Trained in the office, the policy opened forty four of fifty drawers in office scenes, but four of fifty in the house. After two thousand five hundred more steps with house scenes, twenty six of fifty. The bars are ninety five percent intervals. This has not been run on the real robot at home yet.
s12_end: The code, the documentation, and a short course on these ideas are online. Thanks for watching.
